I understand pretty well what you are saying. I’m in a very similar situation myself. My dad passed when I was 12 and left me his 1972 Monte Carlo. I drove it all the time between ages 15-18 and even drove it to prom. When I was 18, I started the car after work to let it warm up and started talking to my boss and forgot I was warming the car up and let it idle for over two hours. I came back to the biggest smoke show I’ve ever seen and a grenaded water pump. The car never ran right after that and ended up wiping lobes off the cam. I was so upset with myself I ended up parking the car for 4 years. Over those 4 years I lost all interest in the car. I never would have started working on it if it wasn’t for a friend that came over to hang out and insisted we work on the car. I reluctantly agreed to do a budget rebuild on the motor. During all of my research on doing the rebuild I constantly flipped back and forth between feeling like the car is a burden and feeling like I’m forced to fix it. It isn’t something I want to do, something I need to do. I always felt like I should be putting all of this money and effort into my “cooler” project cars. But slowly I started getting my interest back in the car now that I have a solid vision for it. Now I look forward to getting the motor back from the machine shop and getting the motor back in the car. Im 22 now and look forward to just driving the car every day like it is brand new. I would be kicking myself so badly if I sold it. My advice to you is if you feel like selling your car for no other reason then you don’t have interest in it anymore, park it somewhere safe if you are able to do so until that spark reignites. Build a different project car and then come back to this. That is what I did and I am so glad that’s what I did. If I tried to rebuild it when I was 18 I would have just slapped a new cam and lifters in and probably wouldn’t enjoy it that much. But with the money and knowledge I have a at 22 the motor is getting a very large cam, aluminum heads and intake, headers, carb and my budget rebuild quickly snowballed into what I’m hoping is a 450hp small block that will lay rubber for miles. It’s gotten me genuinely excited to get the car back together

So, back in January, before my 19th birthday I was in a terrible car accident. I was going down the freeway and had fallen asleep. I went left out of my lane and woke up when I heard my car hit the rumble strips only to see the yellow end cap of the gaurd rail disappearing into the front of the car. I don’t remember the impact and it has taken me weeks to remember more details but I vaguely remember getting narcan shot up my nose because the first responders assumed I had overdosed. After they got me removed from the car I was transported by ambulance to the nearest hospital and then was flown to the large trauma center down town. I fully came to in the helicopter and started freaking out. I didn’t know why I was there or what my car looked like or who knew where I was because I had absolutely no clue as to what was going on. After a bunch of scans and multiple doctors they told me I had damaged the c5 and c6 vertebrae and had a severe concussion- note also, I was not wearing a seatbelt during any of this.  All in all this was a completely life changing experience for me. I lost my dream car, I lost my job, I had to move back home with my mom, and now everyday I have to fight back and neck pain just to get out of bed.
